headline: BNP to announce presidential candidate today after meeting with senior leaders; nomination submission deadline looms
summary: Today marks the final day for submitting presidential election nomination papers. BNP's candidate will be revealed following a crucial meeting between Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and senior party leaders.
details: Today is the last day for submitting nomination papers for the presidential election. The Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) is set to announce its candidate later today.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman will hold a meeting with senior government ministers and BNP leaders at the Secretariat around 12:30 PM. The party's presidential nominee will be declared after this meeting.

BNP plans to submit its nomination papers to the Election Commission (EC) by 1:00 PM. The party's policy-making forum, the National Standing Committee, had previously unanimously entrusted the party chairman with the responsibility of finalizing the candidate.

Sources indicate that BNP is not formally recognizing the Secretariat meeting as a Standing Committee session to avoid controversy. The primary purpose of this gathering is to finalize the proposer and supporter signatures for the nominated candidate.

The party chairman is expected to consult with senior leaders during the meeting to complete this process. One senior leader will act as the proposer, and another as the supporter for the presidential candidate.

Political circles widely speculate that BNP Secretary General Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir is almost certain to be the party's presidential candidate. However, his name has not been officially confirmed by the party as of Wednesday.
Meanwhile, the Jamaat-led 11-party alliance has already announced Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) President Oli Ahmad as their presidential candidate.
caption:
The final day for presidential nominations is here, and BNP is set to reveal its candidate after a high-level meeting. Who will they choose?

Today is the last day for submitting nomination papers for the presidential election. The Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) is set to announce its candidate later today.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman will hold a meeting with senior government ministers and BNP leaders at the Secretariat around 12:30 PM. The party's presidential nominee will be declared after this meeting.

BNP plans to submit its nomination papers to the Election Commission (EC) by 1:00 PM. The party's policy-making forum, the National Standing Committee, had previously unanimously entrusted the party chairman with the responsibility of finalizing the candidate.

Sources indicate that BNP is not formally recognizing the Secretariat meeting as a Standing Committee session to avoid controversy. The primary purpose of this gathering is to finalize the proposer and supporter signatures for the nominated candidate.

The party chairman is expected to consult with senior leaders during the meeting to complete this process. One senior leader will act as the proposer, and another as the supporter for the presidential candidate.

Political circles widely speculate that BNP Secretary General Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir is almost certain to be the party's presidential candidate. However, his name has not been officially confirmed by the party as of Wednesday.

Meanwhile, the Jamaat-led 11-party alliance has already announced Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) President Oli Ahmad as their presidential candidate.

headline: Over 1,000 migrants, including 460 Bangladeshis, arrested in Malaysia in two-day crackdown
summary: Malaysian authorities have detained over a thousand undocumented migrants, including 460 Bangladeshi nationals, during a two-day nationwide operation. The arrests are part of an ongoing crackdown on illegal immigration.
details: Malaysian authorities launched a major crackdown on undocumented migrants across the country. Over a thousand individuals were apprehended within a two-day period as part of this extensive operation.
Among those detained, 460 were identified as Bangladeshi nationals. The arrests highlight the ongoing efforts by Malaysian immigration to control illegal immigration.
caption:
Over 1,000 undocumented migrants, including 460 Bangladeshis, were arrested in Malaysia during a recent two-day operation.

Malaysian authorities launched a major crackdown on undocumented migrants across the country. Over a thousand individuals were apprehended within a two-day period as part of this extensive operation.

Among those detained, 460 were identified as Bangladeshi nationals. The arrests highlight the ongoing efforts by Malaysian immigration to control illegal immigration.
